newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND BOUNCES BACK WITH WORLD CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND BOUNCES BACK WITH WORLD CUP WIN.

text.p: France's Luc Alphand bounced back from his disappointing world championships with victory in the third men's super-G of the Alpine skiing season on Friday.

Alphand, who crashed out of the downhill at the world championships in Sestriere and finished only 12th in the super-G, showed control and composure on one of the most difficult courses on the circuit to clock one minute 15.32 seconds, according to provisional results.
Austrian Hermann Maier pulled off a shock by taking second place from start number 32 in 1:15.87 with Italy's Werner Perathoner third in 1:15.90.

The result marked only the second super-G victory of Alphand's career, after his triumph in the Swiss resort of Laax last month. It allowed the Frenchman to replace Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt at the top of the overall World Cup standings.
Aamodt was unable to make the podium in Friday's race which saw some fast times for the higher start numbers in bright sunshine and warm conditions.
"That was one of the fastest super-Gs I have ever raced," said Alphand who is bidding to become the first Frenchman to win the overall title since Jean-Claude Killy in 1968.
"The World Cup has given me momentum again."
Norway's world champion Atle Skaardal made a mistake at the top of the course when he lost control of one of his skis and he failed to get among the top finishers.
Maier broke his arm earlier in the season but has shown good form in recent training and was not suprised by his second place.
Perathoner's third place with start number 11 was even more remarkable as he had surgery on his left knee at the start of February and was unable to compete in the world championships.
